prize_parts.citation: For developing targeted protein degradation by chemically induced proximity, through heterobifunctional PROTAC degraders and the identification of cereblon as the target of thalidomide-type molecular-glue degraders

statement.case_for: I still regard targeted protein degradation as the game-changer on this list: degrading a protein by bringing it to an E3 ligase, instead of inhibiting it, is a new idea that is chemically simple, has been reproduced in many independent laboratories, and has already changed both laboratory practice (acute protein depletion) and drug discovery. Crews and Deshaies conceived and demonstrated the principle, so the origin of the idea is not in doubt. The round-1 exchange has moved me on the third name. Handa's identification of cereblon as the thalidomide target explains, after decades, why a drug that was already in clinical use works, and shows the same induced-proximity principle operating through a molecular glue. That matters for the maturity question that Brzezinski, Somfai, Sparr and the chair keep raising: the glue strand is the part of the field with an approved drug lineage and real patient outcomes, so a citation that includes it rests on delivered consequences and not only on late-stage trials. Four of the five round-1 supporters of B019 independently chose Handa, and the cases made for him by Aili and Zou are, on the science, stronger than my own argument for Ciulli.
statement.case_against: The credit is still crowded and the cut at three is arbitrary at the margin. Ciulli's VHL ligands and ternary-complex structures turned PROTACs into rational, quantitative design, and he is left out; so are Sakamoto (first PROTAC with Crews and Deshaies), Ito, Gray and Kim. Naming Handa and not Ito, the first author of the cereblon identification, is a real priority question that I cannot settle from the supplied credits. A single citation covering PROTACs and glues risks reading as two discoveries stitched together, and no PROTAC has to my knowledge been approved, so that half of the citation rests on mechanism and clinical-stage evidence.

responses.point: Aili asked for a structural argument that the PROTAC arm alone is the cleaner story, and said that without Handa the prize omits half of the field.
responses.response: I cannot give that argument honestly. The structural case for Ciulli is strong, but it describes optimisation inside a framework that Crews and Deshaies established, whereas cereblon is the discovery of a new target that opened a whole drug class. I accept your point and have moved to Handa. The price is a more demanding citation, which I have tried to keep to one principle (induced proximity to an E3 ligase) realised in two ways, and I still think Ciulli's omission is the weakest point of the trio.

responses.point: Zou said Handa is needed if the committee wants to recognise the mechanism of thalidomide, and that VHL ligand design is a major advance inside the PROTAC framework, while accepting Ciulli for a PROTAC-only citation.
responses.response: This is the distinction that decided it for me. A PROTAC-only citation with Ciulli is internally tidy, but Somfai and Sparr both say it will draw the Handa objection, and I think they are right. Your framing, a new molecular target versus refinement within an established concept, is the cleaner criterion for a three-name cut, and it puts Handa ahead of Ciulli. I would still want the discussion record to say plainly that Ciulli's work is what made PROTACs drug-like.

responses.point: Somfai said a PROTAC-only citation will draw the Handa objection, and that he hesitates to make B019 first because of attribution fragility and the lack of an approved degrader.
responses.response: I agree with the first half and have changed my trio for that reason. On the second, the attribution is less fragile than it looks: all five round-1 supporters name Crews and Deshaies, and the only dispute is the third seat. The absence of an approved PROTAC I treat as a reason for care in the wording, not for deferral, and including the cereblon strand helps there because the thalidomide-derived drugs are in routine clinical use. I still do not think C-N coupling can compete: it extends territory the 2010 prize covered, and B019 opens a new modality.

responses.point: Sparr said B045 is more mature, with approved products and real-world safety data, and that a PROTAC-only B019 grouping with Ciulli would be more coherent than adding glue names.
responses.response: I take the maturity point, and the cereblon strand is my answer to it: the immunomodulatory drugs give B019 a clinical lineage with real-world data, though the PROTAC half remains earlier. I have not followed your preference for the Ciulli grouping because Handa is now the majority's choice and, on the science, the better one. On B045, you flag a second pandemic-themed prize after Medicine 2023 and the crowded Vancouver, Boston and industry credit among Cullis, Hope, Madden, MacLachlan, Anderson and Langer, and I find that credit harder to cut cleanly than B019's.

responses.point: The chair asks whether PROTACs and cereblon glues are one achievement or two, and whether a two-part prize is an option.
responses.response: I regard them as one achievement, chemically induced proximity to an E3 ligase, because both turn an existing protein-destruction pathway into a designable event and both rest on the same ubiquitin ligase machinery. A two-part prize would need four to six names and break the three-laureate limit for any honest crediting, so I would not propose it. If the committee cannot accept a single citation, the fallback is the PROTAC-only citation with Ciulli that I held in round 1, but I do not recommend it.

uncertainties: Whether Ito, as first author of the cereblon identification, has a priority claim that should displace or accompany Handa.
Whether a single citation can honestly cover PROTACs and molecular glues, or whether a PROTAC-only wording with Ciulli would hold up better under scrutiny.
Whether the lack of an approved PROTAC will weigh against the PROTAC half in the final vote.
Whether base editing (B043) becomes the stronger candidate once the Kondo and Nishida priority question is settled.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict or recusal basis for any shortlisted candidate. My connections (Warshel from my postdoc, the Uppsala ribosome and RNA community, long service with Brzezinski) do not touch any credited name, and I have no collaboration with any candidate. This is unchanged from round 1.
